facts.label: Entity and perimeter
facts.text: - The registrant in all four periodic filings is Viasat, Inc., and the statements are consolidated: wholly owned subsidiaries plus the majority-owned subsidiary TrellisWare Technologies, Inc., with a noncontrolling interest in the balance sheet (10-Q June 2026 page:5; balance sheet page:2). The equity-method affiliate JSAT Mobile is outside consolidation (10-Q June 2026 page:43). - Debt is issued in two groups. Viasat, Inc. is the obligor of the 2022 and 2023 Term Loan Facilities, the Viasat Revolving Credit Facility and the 2027, 2028 and 2031 Notes; the Ex-Im Credit Facility is guaranteed by Viasat and secured by the ViaSat-2 satellite and related assets and a pledge of the borrower's capital stock (page:36). The Inmarsat Term Loan Facility, the Inmarsat Revolving Credit Facility and the Inmarsat 2029 Notes belong to the Inmarsat group, guaranteed by certain material Inmarsat subsidiaries and secured by Inmarsat assets (page:35, page:41). The 2027 Notes paragraph describes the Inmarsat 2029 Notes as secured by liens on assets that are not part of the 2027 Notes collateral (page:39). The note text says none of Viasat's subsidiaries guaranteed the 2022 Term Loan, 2023 Term Loan, Revolving Credit, 2027, 2028 or 2031 Notes as of June 30, 2026 (page:32, page:33, page:37, page:38, page:40, page:43). - The filing does not give separate summarized financial statements for the Viasat group and the Inmarsat group, no restricted or unrestricted subsidiary split, and no guarantor financial information. Group-level leverage and the cash held by each group are therefore Not supplied from these sources. This is an unresolved perimeter distinction preserved as a gap. - Amounts in the filings are USD. Statements are in thousands; narrative uses millions or billions; the 10-K text rounds some debt to USD 6.6 billion.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Viasat has deleveraged and improved cover over the past year, but a refinancing event sits close and the headline numbers flatter the run-rate. On the derived basis stated below, total debt to EBITDA is 4.58x for LTM June 2026 against 5.70x for FY2025 and 4.50x for FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA is 3.37x against 4.43x and 3.31x. LTM is slightly worse than FY2026 because the Q1 FY2027 EBITDA is lower than the Q1 FY2026 quarter it replaces while debt fell by only USD 14.6 million between March and June 2026. Gross debt was USD 6,570.5 million at June 30, 2026, of which USD 661.9 million is current, including the USD 600.0 million 5.625% senior secured notes due 2027. Liquidity is USD 1,735.8 million of cash plus USD 1,150.3 million of undrawn revolver availability, but the Inmarsat USD 550.0 million revolver matures on March 28, 2027 and the Viasat revolver carries a springing maturity tied to other material debt. The strongest support is the cash balance, which covers the whole current debt balance, and the 4.73x LTM coverage of cash interest. The weakest point is quality of the base: FY2026 cash flow from operations includes the USD 420.0 million Ligado lump sum and FY2026 other income includes a USD 168.1 million gain on the Navarino sale, and the company prints no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant ratio. What decides the outcome is the 2027 refinancing, the terms of the Viasat revolver springing maturity (conditions not described in the sources), and whether the ViaSat-3 satellites in service lift earnings while capital spending of about USD 1.0 billion a year continues. All metrics below are derived by this analyst from filed GAAP lines and are labelled so; the company's covenant definitions are not supplied.

facts.label: Basis of preparation and definitions
facts.text: - Entity and perimeter: Viasat, Inc. consolidated, which includes wholly owned subsidiaries (the Inmarsat group since May 2023) and the majority-owned TrellisWare Technologies, Inc.; the noncontrolling interest is shown separately (10-Q June 2026 page:5, page:2). Net income attributable to the noncontrolling interest was USD 38,012 thousand in FY2026 (10-K page:129). Consolidated EBITDA below includes 100% of TrellisWare. - Units: USD thousands in the statements; USD millions in MD&A text. Sign convention: outflows and expenses are shown negative in the statement copies below, as the filings print them in parentheses. - Derived EBITDA = Income (loss) from operations + Depreciation + Amortization of intangible assets, the last two from the cash flow statement. No unusual item is added back, stock-based compensation is not added back, and equity income, interest income and other income are excluded. The cash flow amortization line (FY2026 USD 315,950 thousand) is consistent with three disclosed components: acquired intangibles USD 260,712 thousand (10-K page:129), capitalized software USD 41.1 million (10-K page:143) and patents, orbital slots and licenses USD 14.1 million (10-K page:141), which sum to USD 315.9 million within rounding. - Net debt = total debt principal (including finance lease obligations, before unamortized discount and issuance costs) less cash and cash equivalents. Operating leases are outside both debt and net debt; operating lease cost is already deducted in operating income, so derived EBITDA is after lease cost. - Cash interest = cash paid for interest, net of amounts capitalized, from the cash flow supplemental information.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Viasat, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated global satellite communications and defense technology company with two segments and no financial sponsor or parent named in the pack. Communication services (FY2026 revenue USD 3,299.7 million) sells aviation, government satcom, maritime and fixed broadband connectivity from an owned fleet of 23 in-service or operational satellites; defense and advanced technologies (USD 1,340.6 million) sells encryption, tactical networking and space systems to governments. For a creditor the business is recurring in services, which are 71% of FY2026 revenue, but its cash needs are driven by roughly USD 1.0 billion a year of capital spending and by satellite programs that have already cost it: the ViaSat-3 F1 reflector issue left less than 10% of throughput recovered and led to a net loss of about USD 905.5 million in FY2024. The defining transaction is the May 2023 Inmarsat acquisition for about USD 2.7 billion of consideration, which created a second, separately financed debt group; in the last two fiscal years the documented actions are repayment (the 2025 Notes redeemed in May 2025, the Original Inmarsat Term Loan repaid early in November 2025, total debt down from USD 7,204.3 million to USD 6,570.5 million) and asset sales (the Navarino UK interest for USD 203.0 million in March 2026), with no dividend ever declared. Strongest support: diversified commercial customers, a firm backlog of USD 4,217.7 million at June 30, 2026, and the in-flight connectivity base of about 4,630 aircraft. Weakest points: concentration in the U.S. Government at 16% of FY2026 revenue and five contracts at 19%, the incomplete ownership picture, and the 2027 refinancing. What decides the outcome is whether ViaSat-3 F2 and F3 reach commercial service as expected and lift revenue while spending falls, and how the 2027 Notes and the Inmarsat revolver expiring in March 2027 are handled. The pack ends at June 30, 2026, so whether the satellites entered service on the expected dates is not evidenced. Ownership, control rights and sponsor behaviour cannot be judged beyond the facts below because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The principal transaction in the evidence is the Inmarsat acquisition, completed on May 30, 2023 and described by the company as the purchase of Connect Topco Limited, a private Guernsey company, "in exchange for approximately $550.7 million in cash and 46.36 million shares of our common stock" (10-K page:6). The 10-K states total consideration of about USD 2.7 billion, comprising USD 2.1 billion of fair value of the shares and USD 550.7 million in cash, with goodwill of USD 1.5 billion in communication services (10-K page:169-170) and USD 31.3 million of transaction costs in FY2024. The financing of that deal and of Inmarsat since then is visible in the debt record: the 2023 Term Loan Facility of USD 616.7 million was entered into at the closing (10-Q June 2026 page:33), the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2031 of USD 733.4 million were issued in September 2023 to replace a USD 733.4 million unsecured bridge facility (page:42), Inmarsat amended its facilities in March 2024 to establish a USD 1.3 billion Inmarsat Term Loan Facility and a USD 550.0 million revolver (page:34), and certain Inmarsat Holdings subsidiaries issued USD 1.975 billion of 9.000% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 in September 2024 (page:41), the proceeds of which, with cash, redeemed all of the remaining USD 1.97 billion of Inmarsat 2026 Notes (10-K page:181). Status of the transaction: completed, with the share issuance of about 46.36 million shares and a role rationalization of about 800 positions that management announced as complete in November 2023 and describes as intended to achieve operational and cost efficiencies (10-K page:110; Management Language).

facts.text: New debt and debt events in the periods since FY2025, all completed: in May 2025 the remaining USD 442.6 million of 5.625% Senior Notes due 2025 were redeemed at par (10-Q June 2026 page:38); in November 2025 the USD 300.0 million Original Inmarsat Term Loan was repaid early (page:34); on January 21, 2026 Viasat and ViaSat Technologies Limited entered into a USD 188.7 million direct loan facility with the Export-Import Bank of the United States, fully drawn at USD 188.7 million at March 31, 2026, repayable in 16 semi-annual installments from May 2026 to November 25, 2033 (10-Q Dec 2025 page:56; 10-K page:178); the former Ex-Im facility was repaid at maturity on October 15, 2025 (10-K page:178). No new debt was issued in Q1 FY2027 and no financing is described after June 30, 2026 in the sources. facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: services were 71% of FY2026 revenue, connectivity contracts require "advance or recurring monthly payments" (10-Q June 2026 page:6), firm backlog stood at USD 4,217.7 million, and aviation services revenue rose from USD 1,048,225 thousand to USD 1,191,426 thousand in FY2026 (10-K page:205). Risk mechanic: recurring service billing and a growing in-flight connectivity base (about 4,630 aircraft) support revenue visibility and cash conversion, but fixed services revenue fell from USD 741,601 thousand to USD 607,693 thousand as bandwidth was reallocated to aviation (10-K page:106), so growth depends on a shrinking consumer line being replaced. Credit implication: supports debt service capacity and refinancing access, tempered by capacity constraints before new satellites enter service; the backlog excludes future recurring IFC revenue (10-K page:108), so it understates aviation visibility. The Q1 FY2027 revenue decline (product revenues fell) is a counter-signal, small in size. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: capital expenditure of USD 992,774 thousand in FY2026, a USD 169.4 million impairment and other liabilities for the EMEA exit in FY2025, and in FY2024 a reduction of about USD 1.67 billion in the carrying value of satellites under construction, partly offset by about USD 770.0 million of insurance claim receivables (10-K page:137). Risk mechanic: owned-satellite capital intensity and launch or anomaly risk absorb cash flow ahead of revenue, and management itself expects higher operating costs before new satellites reach commercial service (10-Q June 2026 page:74). Credit implication: free cash flow depends on capital spending falling as satellites complete; FY2026 cash flow also benefited from the Ligado lump sum and the Navarino proceeds (CP-1), so run-rate debt service coverage is weaker than the headline. The ViaSat-3 F1 reflector issue is the documented precedent for execution risk. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: U.S. Government 16% of FY2026 revenue and five largest contracts 19%; "A majority of our contracts can be terminated at the convenience of the customer" (10-Q June 2026 page:69); DCAA is auditing fiscal 2025 incurred costs (page:9). Risk mechanic: government funding delays, audits and termination rights can interrupt cash receipts and revise revenue; a USD 15.1 million reserve exists for refunds. Credit implication: moderate concentration that matters most in a downturn or shutdown; no single commercial customer reaches 10%. 4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, repayment actions, no distributions beyond TrellisWare's minority. Risk mechanic: absent a controlling owner with a distribution incentive, leakage risk to creditors is low on documented actions, but ownership concentration and board rights are Not disclosed. Credit implication: alignment appears neutral to supportive on documented actions only; willingness is not inferred from identity. Counter-evidence: the Cooperation Agreement of May 2026 is unexplained and could alter board composition; its terms are Not supplied. 5. Structure and key uncertainties. Evidence: two debt groups with separate collateral and guarantors (CP-1), the Inmarsat revolver maturing March 28, 2027, the 2027 Notes in current debt, and a Viasat revolver with a springing maturity. Risk mechanic: creditor claims are structurally separated, so group-level cash and leverage drive recoveries and refinancing choices, and the springing date can remove revolver availability early. Credit implication: refinancing timing and group-level disclosure are the key uncertainties; recovery prospects cannot be assessed beyond noting the liens described, and no recovery conclusion is made.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Viasat's credit is adequate but exposed: debt has fallen and liquidity is ample, yet a USD 600.0 million secured-note maturity falls due by mid-2027 and cash generation depends on satellite spending easing. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,886.1 million and a recurring services base, with gross leverage down to 4.58x on derived EBITDA for the twelve months to June 2026 from 5.70x in FY2025. The weakest point is thin earnings after spending: derived EBITDA less capital expenditure was only 1.39x cash interest, and operating income covers just 0.32x of interest expense. What decides the outcome is whether the ViaSat-3 satellites lift revenue while capital spending of about USD 1.0 billion a year falls, and how the 2027 Notes and the Inmarsat revolver are refinanced.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Viasat's total debt was USD 6,570.5 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 7,204.3 million at March 31, 2025, and gross leverage is 4.58x with net leverage 3.37x on derived, unadjusted EBITDA of USD 1,435.6 million for the twelve months, against 5.70x gross and 4.43x net in FY2025. The 5.625% Senior Secured Notes of USD 600.0 million are in current debt at June 30, 2026, and the fiscal-year schedule places them between April and June 2027 by inference. The larger wall follows: USD 3,246.7 million falls in FY2030 and USD 1,341.3 million in FY2031. The reported cash flow flatters the run-rate. FY2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,589.9 million includes the Ligado lump sum of USD 420.0 million, leaving about USD 177.1 million of free cash flow for FY2026 and about USD 158.3 million for the twelve months, against reported USD 597.1 million and USD 578.3 million. FY2026 other income also includes the USD 168.1 million Navarino gain, which is outside derived EBITDA. A further USD 100 million Ligado payment remains outstanding with no collection date. 6. Business risk is moderate. Services are 71% of FY2026 revenue and firm backlog is USD 4,217.7 million, aviation services revenue rose in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027, and no commercial customer reaches 10% of revenue; against that, the U.S. Government is 16% of FY2026 revenue, the five largest contracts are 19%, product revenue fell in Q1 FY2027, and derived EBITDA for Q1 FY2027 was USD 361.3 million against USD 388.3 million a year earlier. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Deleveraging: total debt is USD 633.8 million lower than at March 2025 and derived coverage of cash interest rose from 3.24x to 4.73x (Documentary Fact, CP-1 figures; the ratios are derived, so read as Analyst Interpretation of filed lines). (3) Recurring services base and backlog: services are 71% of revenue, connectivity is billed in advance or monthly, and firm backlog is USD 4,217.7 million (Documentary Fact; the backlog excludes future recurring in-flight connectivity revenue, so visibility is understated). (4) Customer breadth: no commercial customer at 10% of revenue and the in-flight connectivity base of about 4,630 aircraft is growing (Documentary Fact). (5) Segment balance: defense and advanced technologies earned segment operating profit of USD 216.3 million in FY2026, steady with the prior year, beside a communication services swing to profit that mainly reflects the absence of the FY2025 EMEA impairment (Documentary Fact). (6) Creditor-supportive actions: debt repaid and no dividends (Documentary Fact for the actions; the inference that they signal willingness is Analyst Interpretation).

spans.text: ## Request

VIASAT INC (registrant Viasat, Inc., Nasdaq: VSAT; Delaware; Carlsbad, California) is the issuer. As-of date: 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot, host session (this analyst answers; no provider call). Scope: a source-readiness review of the seven pinned issuer files for the selected consumers CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. Reporting currency per the run context: USD (the filed statements are in USD thousands; MD&A text uses USD millions and billions). Fiscal year ends March 31, so the context's current period q1-2027 is the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY2027) and its prior period fy-2026 is the year ended March 31, 2026 (FY2026). This module gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes and reconciles nothing.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
All seven are retained, each is a text extraction of an SEC filing. No source was blocked in preparation. The sha256 values are those of the extracted text files CP-OS pinned for this run.

### Supplied handoffs
None. CP-0 is the first module of this run, so CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff, and none is relied on.
### External sources
None. No outside knowledge of the company was used.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven pinned files support the financial, business and evidence-trace work, with bounded limitations. The three results releases add no figures, so every number must come from the 10-K and three 10-Qs. | Medium | No EBITDA or covenant definitions, no covenant levels, no legal documents, and no discrete fourth-quarter statements. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited annual and three interim statements, debt and liquidity notes are present, in USD thousands for fiscal years ending March 31. | Debt, liquidity and maturity analysis can start from filed figures. | High |
| The results releases carry only call logistics and no financial tables or slides. | Management adjusted metrics and guidance cannot be tested against filings. | High |
| Covenant tests are named for the revolvers and Ex-Im loan but no levels or reported ratios appear. | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed from these files. | High |
| Debt sits in separate Viasat and Inmarsat groups, and one-off items distort fiscal 2026. | Leverage and coverage need group-level and normalized views, with care. | Medium |
| Ownership, governance and the Cooperation Agreement terms are not in the pack. | Control and shareholder-influence points stay open. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient to start all four selected consumers: the audited FY2026 10-K and the three 10-Qs through June 30, 2026 carry full statements, a facility-level debt note, liquidity text, segment and backlog tables, leases and commitments, so source sufficiency holds for CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. The strongest contrary evidence is what the pack lacks: the three Exhibit 99.1 files are call-logistics notices with no financial content, so no management reconciliation, adjusted measure or guidance is supplied (page:1 of each); no filing prints EBITDA or any covenant ratio level; credit agreements and indentures are listed only as exhibit titles, not supplied; and Q4 FY2026 and the June 2025 quarter are not stand-alone statements. These gaps limit add-back, covenant and discrete-quarter work, but do not stop the consumers, which can build metrics from filed GAAP lines and flag the rest. This is source sufficiency only; the model input contract is not evaluated here, and no downstream analysis has been completed or accepted. The next evidence action is to obtain the shareholder letters and webcast slides for the three releases, the credit agreements and indentures for the Viasat and Inmarsat groups, and the proxy statement.
Consumer assessment (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED):
| Consumer | Readiness | Evidence it needs and where it sits | Bounded limitations carried forward |

| CP-1 financial base | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual statements page:128-131; quarterly statements page:2-4 of each 10-Q; debt note page:173-186 of the 10-K and page:32-43 of the June 2026 10-Q; liquidity page:69-72 and page:75 of the June 2026 10-Q; segments page:48 and page:205 | No EBITDA or add-back schedule; cash flows are year-to-date only in the interim filings; fourth quarter is not a stand-alone statement; covenant levels absent |

| CP-1A business and transaction | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, fleet and Inmarsat acquisition in the 10-K (Item 1, page:5-41 and Note 4, page:168-170); backlog page:68; Ligado page:46; ownership and governance incorporated by reference to a proxy statement (page:119-120) | Proxy statement and the May 6, 2026 Cooperation Agreement not supplied; sponsor and shareholder control cannot be read from the pack |

| CP-2 credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Draws on the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs only; the filed evidence for both is present | Inherits every limitation above; a missing handoff is sequenced by the planner and is not a source condition |

| CP-5 evidence trace | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Needs retrievable quotes for all claims; all seven sources are text-extracted and quotable | Extraction success is not a fidelity review; tables were extracted with values split across lines, so figures need checking against their locators |
No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, so the command sheet has no DO NOT RUN entry.
### Source assessment
#### Entity and perimeter

- The registrant in all four periodic filings is Viasat, Inc., and the statements are consolidated: wholly owned subsidiaries plus the majority-owned subsidiary TrellisWare Technologies, Inc., with a noncontrolling interest in the balance sheet (10-Q June 2026 page:5; balance sheet page:2). The equity-method affiliate JSAT Mobile is outside consolidation (10-Q June 2026 page:43).

- Debt is issued in two groups. Viasat, Inc. is the obligor of the 2022 and 2023 Term Loan Facilities, the Viasat Revolving Credit Facility and the 2027, 2028 and 2031 Notes; the Ex-Im Credit Facility is guaranteed by Viasat and secured by the ViaSat-2 satellite and related assets and a pledge of the borrower's capital stock (page:36). The Inmarsat Term Loan Facility, the Inmarsat Revolving Credit Facility and the Inmarsat 2029 Notes belong to the Inmarsat group, guaranteed by certain material Inmarsat subsidiaries and secured by Inmarsat assets (page:35, page:41). The 2027 Notes paragraph describes the Inmarsat 2029 Notes as secured by liens on assets that are not part of the 2027 Notes collateral (page:39). The note text says none of Viasat's subsidiaries guaranteed the 2022 Term Loan, 2023 Term Loan, Revolving Credit, 2027, 2028 or 2031 Notes as of June 30, 2026 (page:32, page:33, page:37, page:38, page:40, page:43).

- The filing does not give separate summarized financial statements for the Viasat group and the Inmarsat group, no restricted or unrestricted subsidiary split, and no guarantor financial information. Group-level leverage and the cash held by each group are therefore Not supplied from these sources. This is an unresolved perimeter distinction preserved as a gap.
- Amounts in the filings are USD. Statements are in thousands; narrative uses millions or billions; the 10-K text rounds some debt to USD 6.6 billion.
#### Annual report (10-K, FY2026)

- Contains audited balance sheet (page:128-129), statements of operations (page:129-130), cash flows with cash paid for interest and taxes (page:130-131), and the notes: leases (page:172), senior notes and other long-term debt with a fiscal-year maturity table (page:173), segment information (page:203-206), commitments (page:200-201) and contingencies (page:201-202).
- The auditor's opinion covers the financial statements and internal control over financial reporting, with a critical audit matter on communication services revenue recognition (page:125-128).

- Items that make FY2026 not a clean run-rate and that downstream modules must treat deliberately: the cash flow statement carries a gain on sale of an equity interest in an unconsolidated affiliate of 168,062 thousand (page:130; Navarino UK sale in March 2026, page:200), a loss on extinguishment of debt of 11,935 thousand (page:130), and the income statement shows interest income of 205,849 thousand against 83,920 thousand in FY2025 (page:129).
#### Interim reports (10-Q, Q2 FY2026, Q3 FY2026, Q1 FY2027)

- Each carries a balance sheet, statements of operations, cash flows, equity, notes, MD&A, and exhibit lists. Discrete quarters can be read directly from the income statements for Q2 FY2026 (three months, September 30, 2025), Q3 FY2026 (three months, December 31, 2025) and Q1 FY2027 with Q1 FY2026 as comparative. Cash flows are presented six months (September 30, 2025 filing page:3-4) and nine months (December 31, 2025 filing page:3-4) year to date; only Q1 FY2027 and Q1 FY2026 cash flows are three-month figures (June 2026 filing page:3-4).

- Q4 FY2026 is not reported stand-alone; the annual figures and nine-month figures would have to be differenced, and the June 2025 10-Q is not in the pack (Q1 FY2026 appears only as comparative columns in the June 2026 10-Q). A difference is a derivation, not a source fact, and must be labelled so.

- The Q3 FY2026 income statement contains a Ligado-related item that the filing ties to the lump sum payment: the December 2025 10-Q states that 152.5 million of the Ligado lump sum was recognized as interest income and 267.5 million as deferred revenue (page:52), and that the 147.9 million increase in interest income for the quarter was primarily this item (page:74).
#### Results releases (Exhibit 99.1, three files)

- Each file is a short announcement of results and call details, with company boilerplate and contacts. It states that a letter to shareholders and webcast slides are posted on the company's investor site, but these are not in the pack (page:1 of each file). The files contain no reported or adjusted figures, reconciliations, quarter versus year-to-date tables or guidance. They provide dates of the announcements only and cannot be used as quantitative evidence. This is a coverage gap for management narrative and any adjusted metric, and it does not weaken the filed statements.
- The pack lists them as releases standing in for presentations (no deck was retrieved); no slide or speaker-note coverage is claimed.
#### Debt, liquidity and covenants (filed text)

- The 10-Q for June 30, 2026 lists total debt of 6,570,503 thousand by facility against 6,585,115 thousand at March 31, 2026, with current portion of 661,939 thousand against 57,753 thousand (page:32). The 10-K gives the same March 31, 2026 total and a fiscal-year maturity table (page:173).

- Liquidity text: cash and cash equivalents of 1,735,819 thousand (page:2); Viasat revolver 647.5 million with 47.2 million of standby letters of credit and 600.3 million available (page:37); Inmarsat revolver 550.0 million undrawn, maturing March 28, 2027 (page:34). The 10-Q contractual obligations table is on page:75.

- Covenants: the revolvers and the Ex-Im Credit Facility have a maximum total leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio (page:36-37), and the Inmarsat revolver carries total net leverage and interest coverage tests (page:35). The filings state compliance as of June 30, 2026. No threshold, step-down, reported ratio or covenant EBITDA definition is printed, so headroom is Not calculable from these sources.

- Calendar maturity dates for the 2027, 2028, Inmarsat 2029 and 2031 Notes are not printed in the sources reviewed (only the year in the title and fiscal-year buckets in the 10-K table). The term loans, the Inmarsat revolver, the Viasat revolver (with its springing maturity) and the Ex-Im facility have printed dates (page:32-37).
#### Segment, KPI and backlog

- Two reportable segments, communication services and defense and advanced technologies, with business-line revenue, segment expenses and segment operating profit (June 2026 10-Q page:48; 10-K page:205). Segment assets are not presented because the chief operating decision maker is not provided them (page:49). Firm and funded backlog by segment is on page:68 of the June 2026 10-Q. Aircraft in service counts are on page:53.

- Add-backs: depreciation, amortization, stock-based compensation, and acquisition and transaction expenses appear in the cash flow and segment tables, but no company-defined adjusted measure exists in any pack file.
#### Version and relationship notes

- The June 2026 10-Q and the 10-K are different periods of one reporting line, not versions of each other, and all remain active. Figures I cross-checked agree: the March 31, 2026 total debt of 6,585,115 thousand and cash of 1,746,835 thousand appear in both the 10-K and the June 2026 10-Q comparative column.

- One wording difference is a progression, not a conflict: the 10-K says the DCMA had approved incurred costs through fiscal year 2022 (page:202) and the June 2026 10-Q says through fiscal year 2023 (page:9).

- The December 2025 10-Q reported the Ex-Im loan facility of 188.7 million as a subsequent event of January 21, 2026 (page:56); the 10-K and June 2026 10-Q describe the same facility as outstanding. This is consistent. Neither the 10-K notes (Notes 1 to 16) nor the June 2026 10-Q notes (Notes 1 to 10) include a subsequent-events note. The Cooperation Agreement dated May 6, 2026 appears only as an exhibit title (10-K page:124), and its terms are not supplied.

- No draft, unsigned or superseded document is in the pack. Nothing dated after the cutoff of 2026-11-05 is used: the latest source is the 10-Q for June 30, 2026 and the announcement of August 4, 2026.
### Gap register
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |
| Shareholder letters and webcast slides for the three results releases are not in the pack | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Add them to the pack |

| No EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or free cash flow measure, and no add-back schedule, is printed in any filing | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Build from filed GAAP lines and label as derived, or obtain the releases |

| Covenant levels, step-downs, definitions and reported ratios are not printed; credit agreements and indentures are not supplied | High for covenant work, Low for others | CP-2, CP-5 | Add the executed agreements for the Viasat and Inmarsat groups |

| No separate financial information for the Viasat group and the Inmarsat group, restricted group or guarantors | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Add group-level disclosure or the agreements' compliance information |
| Q4 FY2026 and Q1 FY2026 are not stand-alone statements; interim cash flows are year to date | Low | CP-1 | Derive by difference and label |
| Proxy statement, ownership of securities and Cooperation Agreement terms not supplied | Medium | CP-1A | Add the proxy and the May 2026 8-K exhibit |
| Calendar maturity dates of the 2027, 2028, Inmarsat 2029 and 2031 Notes not printed in the reviewed text | Low | CP-1, CP-2 | Add the indentures |
## Calculations
No new calculation is made, because CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Counts only:
- Pinned issuer sources: 7 (4 periodic filings, 3 press release exhibits). Extracted pages: 206 + 91 + 93 + 81 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 474.

- Pages individually read for this assessment: cover and contents, the primary statements, the debt, liquidity, contractual obligations, segment, backlog, lease, commitment, contingency, subsequent-event and exhibit-list pages, Part III, and the three release files. Pages not individually read are risk factors, regulation, most business narrative, tax, equity compensation, retirement-plan and similar notes, and the signature and certification pages. They are retained and quotable but not assessed, and no claim of full-page review is made.

- Cross-check with no derived figure: the fiscal-year debt maturity table (page:173 of the 10-K) states a total of 6,585,115 thousand, equal to the March 31, 2026 total debt in the 10-Q table (page:32).
## Gaps
- Not supplied: management adjusted measures and guidance, because the release files carry no financial content.
- Not calculable: covenant headroom, because no level, definition or reported ratio is printed. Group-level leverage for Viasat and Inmarsat, because no group-level statements are printed.

- Not supplied: executed credit agreements, indentures, intercreditor terms and collateral schedules. Legal interpretation is outside this module and the legal documents status in the run context is none.
- Not supplied: proxy statement and shareholder ownership data; terms of the Cooperation Agreement of May 6, 2026.

- Unresolved: whether the 100 million Ligado payment due March 2026, shown as still outstanding pending resolution of certain matters at June 30, 2026 (page:46), is collected; the filing gives no collection date.

- Parse limits: sources are text extractions of HTML filings. Tables survive as line-separated values with negative signs split across lines, and charts or images, if any, were not inspected; no fidelity review against the original HTML was performed.

- Currency and period: all statements are USD with a March 31 fiscal year end, matching the context; no other currency or period basis is reported as the reporting basis. Some operations are conducted in foreign currencies (June 2026 10-Q page:78), but figures are reported in USD.
## Next module

CP-1 (financial base) is next. It should open the statements and debt note at the locators above, label derived quarters and year-to-date cash flows, keep the Viasat and Inmarsat debt groups separate, flag the Ligado interest income of Q3 FY2026 and the Navarino gain in FY2026 as unusual items needing separate treatment, and carry forward the missing EBITDA, covenant and group-level disclosure as explicit gaps. CP-1A follows for business and transaction context, using the 10-K business pages and the Inmarsat acquisition note, and treating ownership and governance as Insufficient Information until a proxy statement is supplied.

### Financial base view

Viasat has deleveraged and improved cover over the past year, but a refinancing event sits close and the headline numbers flatter the run-rate. On the derived basis stated below, total debt to EBITDA is 4.58x for LTM June 2026 against 5.70x for FY2025 and 4.50x for FY2026, and net debt to EBITDA is 3.37x against 4.43x and 3.31x. LTM is slightly worse than FY2026 because the Q1 FY2027 EBITDA is lower than the Q1 FY2026 quarter it replaces while debt fell by only USD 14.6 million between March and June 2026. Gross debt was USD 6,570.5 million at June 30, 2026, of which USD 661.9 million is current, including the USD 600.0 million 5.625% senior secured notes due 2027. Liquidity is USD 1,735.8 million of cash plus USD 1,150.3 million of undrawn revolver availability, but the Inmarsat USD 550.0 million revolver matures on March 28, 2027 and the Viasat revolver carries a springing maturity tied to other material debt. The strongest support is the cash balance, which covers the whole current debt balance, and the 4.73x LTM coverage of cash interest. The weakest point is quality of the base: FY2026 cash flow from operations includes the USD 420.0 million Ligado lump sum and FY2026 other income includes a USD 168.1 million gain on the Navarino sale, and the company prints no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant ratio. What decides the outcome is the 2027 refinancing, the terms of the Viasat revolver springing maturity (conditions not described in the sources), and whether the ViaSat-3 satellites in service lift earnings while capital spending of about USD 1.0 billion a year continues. All metrics below are derived by this analyst from filed GAAP lines and are labelled so; the company's covenant definitions are not supplied.
### Basis of preparation and definitions

- Entity and perimeter: Viasat, Inc. consolidated, which includes wholly owned subsidiaries (the Inmarsat group since May 2023) and the majority-owned TrellisWare Technologies, Inc.; the noncontrolling interest is shown separately (10-Q June 2026 page:5, page:2). Net income attributable to the noncontrolling interest was USD 38,012 thousand in FY2026 (10-K page:129). Consolidated EBITDA below includes 100% of TrellisWare.
- Units: USD thousands in the statements; USD millions in MD&A text. Sign convention: outflows and expenses are shown negative in the statement copies below, as the filings print them in parentheses.

- Derived EBITDA = Income (loss) from operations + Depreciation + Amortization of intangible assets, the last two from the cash flow statement. No unusual item is added back, stock-based compensation is not added back, and equity income, interest income and other income are excluded. The cash flow amortization line (FY2026 USD 315,950 thousand) is consistent with three disclosed components: acquired intangibles USD 260,712 thousand (10-K page:129), capitalized software USD 41.1 million (10-K page:143) and patents, orbital slots and licenses USD 14.1 million (10-K page:141), which sum to USD 315.9 million within rounding.

- Net debt = total debt principal (including finance lease obligations, before unamortized discount and issuance costs) less cash and cash equivalents. Operating leases are outside both debt and net debt; operating lease cost is already deducted in operating income, so derived EBITDA is after lease cost.
- Cash interest = cash paid for interest, net of amounts capitalized, from the cash flow supplemental information.

### Maturity wall

Fiscal-year principal maturities at March 31, 2026 (10-K page:173), USD thousands, including finance leases and before USD 136,510 thousand of unamortized discount and costs: FY2027 57,753; FY2028 655,322; FY2029 1,108,693; FY2030 3,246,671; FY2031 1,341,337; thereafter 175,339; total 6,585,115. FY2028 holds the USD 600,000 thousand 2027 Notes. At June 30, 2026 the current portion is 661,939 thousand (10-Q June 2026 page:2), which includes the 2027 Notes (page:38). Taken together, the 10-K bucket and the current classification place the 2027 Notes between April 1 and June 30, 2027; this is an inference from two disclosures, as the maturity date itself is not printed. FY2030 carries the largest bucket at USD 3,246,671 thousand; by printed date it holds the Inmarsat Term Loan (September 28, 2029), and its size is consistent with the Inmarsat 2029 Notes also falling there, although their date is not printed. The 2023 Term Loan (May 30, 2030) falls in FY2031. The 10-Q for June 2026 does not restate a fiscal-year maturity table.

### Covenants

The filings name the tests but print no thresholds, step-downs or reported ratios. The Viasat Revolving Credit Facility has a maximum total leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio (10-Q June 2026 page:37). The Ex-Im Credit Facility has a maximum total leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio (page:36). The Inmarsat revolver has total net leverage and interest coverage covenants applying to Inmarsat (page:35). The term loans and the notes carry incurrence-style restrictions on debt, liens, asset sales, investments and restricted payments (page:33, page:39-43). The company states compliance with all of them as of June 30, 2026 (page:33-37). Headroom is Not calculable: the covenant levels and the covenant definitions of EBITDA, debt and interest are Not supplied, and the credit agreements are not in the pack. The derived leverage and coverage here must not be read as covenant ratios, and the covenant tests for the Viasat borrower group and the Inmarsat group would each use a different perimeter from the consolidated figures.

### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow in FY2026 of USD 1,589,885 thousand includes the Ligado lump sum: management attributes the year-on-year increase largely to higher deferred revenues from the USD 420.0 million receipt (10-K page:112). Free cash flow, derived as operating cash flow less purchases of property, equipment and satellites, was USD (121,995) thousand in FY2025, USD 597,111 thousand in FY2026, USD 578,286 thousand for LTM June 2026 and USD 41,622 thousand in Q1 FY2027 against USD 60,447 thousand in Q1 FY2026. Removing the USD 420.0 million lump sum, which this analyst does as a labelled sensitivity and not as a normalization, gives about USD 177.1 million for FY2026 and about USD 158.3 million for LTM. The revenue recognized each period from the USD 267.5 million deferred allocation is Not supplied (searched Ligado with revenue in all four periodic filings). Other flows that matter: proceeds from the Navarino sale of USD 202,958 thousand were investing, not operating (10-K page:130); satellite insurance proceeds were USD 10,000 thousand in FY2026 and USD 251,500 thousand in FY2025 (page:130), and none in Q1 FY2027. Capital expenditure was USD 992,774 thousand in FY2026 and management expects fiscal 2027 to be flat to slightly down (10-K page:113). Interest paid is net of capitalized interest, which increased in FY2026 (10-K page:105), so cash interest understates gross interest cost.

All inputs are from the cited filings in USD thousands unless stated; each result is rounded for presentation as shown.
1. Derived EBITDA = income (loss) from operations + depreciation + amortization of intangible assets.

2. Quarterly derivations: Q2 FY2026 depreciation 510,371 - 257,701 = 252,670 and amortization 157,578 - 83,965 = 73,613 (six-month cash flow, 10-Q Sep 2025 page:3-4); Q3 FY2026 depreciation 771,528 - 510,371 = 261,157 and amortization 236,276 - 157,578 = 78,698 (nine-month, 10-Q Dec 2025 page:3-4); Q4 FY2026 revenue 4,640,280 - 3,468,992 = 1,171,288, operating income 108,125 - 108,749 = -624, depreciation 1,038,515 - 771,528 = 266,987 and amortization 315,950 - 236,276 = 79,674.

7. Sensitivity, not a metric of record: adding back the USD 169.4 million FY2025 ground network net loss (10-K page:104) to FY2025 EBITDA gives 1,263.3 + 169.4 = 1,432.7 and total debt / EBITDA of 7,204.3 / 1,432.7 = 5.03 and net 5,592.2 / 1,432.7 = 3.90.
## Gaps

- Not supplied: company-defined EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or any add-back schedule; all EBITDA here is derived and unadjusted. The shareholder letters and slides that the three release notices mention are not in the pack.

- Not calculable: covenant headroom for any facility, because thresholds, definitions and reported ratios are not printed. Group-level leverage and cash for the Viasat group and the Inmarsat group, because no group-level statements are printed.

- Not supplied: the day and month of maturity of the 2027, 2028, Inmarsat 2029 and 2031 Notes, and the conditions that trigger the Viasat revolver springing maturity; the 2027 Notes maturity is inferred only to the window April 1 to June 30, 2027.

- Not supplied: the revenue recognized each period from the USD 267.5 million Ligado deferred allocation, and the cash timing of quarterly Ligado payments beyond the stated approximately USD 16 million a quarter with a 3% annual escalator.

- Q4 FY2026 and the cash flows of Q2 and Q3 FY2026 are derived by difference, not reported; the June 2025 10-Q is not in the pack and Q1 FY2026 comes from comparative columns. The LTM cash interest uses two quarters rounded to USD 0.1 million.

- Unusual items are left inside derived EBITDA except in the labelled sensitivity: ground network impairment in FY2025, loss on disposition of fixed assets (USD 22,770 thousand in FY2026 per the cash flow caption), stock-based compensation (USD 81,070 thousand in FY2026) and acquisition and transaction expenses. No normalization is made.
- Unresolved: USD 100 million Ligado payment outstanding at June 30, 2026 with no collection date; unrecognized tax benefits of USD 230.9 million; no pension or factoring disclosures located.

- Currency and period: all figures are USD and fiscal years end March 31, matching the context. This module corrects nothing in the CP-0 handoff; it adds the maturity inference and the quantified Ligado and Navarino items that CP-0 only flagged.
## Next module

CP-1A (business and transaction context) should use the Inmarsat acquisition, the Ligado settlement, the Navarino sale and the satellite programme as transaction facts, with the derived metrics and the unusual items above as the financial context. CP-2 should carry the leverage, coverage, liquidity and maturity metrics only as derived and unadjusted, treat the 2027 refinancing and the Inmarsat revolver expiry as the near-term events, and keep covenant headroom and group-level leverage as open gaps until the credit agreements and group disclosures are supplied.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Viasat is a satellite and defense group with no identified sponsor or controlling holder. Creditor risk centres on satellite spending, a two-group debt structure from the Inmarsat deal, government concentration and a near-term refinancing. | Medium | Ownership percentages, governance documents and the cooperation agreement are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Revenue is mostly services, led by aviation, with the U.S. Government at 16% of FY2026 revenue and the five largest contracts at 19%. | Service revenue is recurring, but government funding and a few contracts add concentration risk. | High |

### Business and transaction view

Viasat, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated global satellite communications and defense technology company with two segments and no financial sponsor or parent named in the pack. Communication services (FY2026 revenue USD 3,299.7 million) sells aviation, government satcom, maritime and fixed broadband connectivity from an owned fleet of 23 in-service or operational satellites; defense and advanced technologies (USD 1,340.6 million) sells encryption, tactical networking and space systems to governments. For a creditor the business is recurring in services, which are 71% of FY2026 revenue, but its cash needs are driven by roughly USD 1.0 billion a year of capital spending and by satellite programs that have already cost it: the ViaSat-3 F1 reflector issue left less than 10% of throughput recovered and led to a net loss of about USD 905.5 million in FY2024. The defining transaction is the May 2023 Inmarsat acquisition for about USD 2.7 billion of consideration, which created a second, separately financed debt group; in the last two fiscal years the documented actions are repayment (the 2025 Notes redeemed in May 2025, the Original Inmarsat Term Loan repaid early in November 2025, total debt down from USD 7,204.3 million to USD 6,570.5 million) and asset sales (the Navarino UK interest for USD 203.0 million in March 2026), with no dividend ever declared. Strongest support: diversified commercial customers, a firm backlog of USD 4,217.7 million at June 30, 2026, and the in-flight connectivity base of about 4,630 aircraft. Weakest points: concentration in the U.S. Government at 16% of FY2026 revenue and five contracts at 19%, the incomplete ownership picture, and the 2027 refinancing. What decides the outcome is whether ViaSat-3 F2 and F3 reach commercial service as expected and lift revenue while spending falls, and how the 2027 Notes and the Inmarsat revolver expiring in March 2027 are handled. The pack ends at June 30, 2026, so whether the satellites entered service on the expected dates is not evidenced. Ownership, control rights and sponsor behaviour cannot be judged beyond the facts below because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The principal transaction in the evidence is the Inmarsat acquisition, completed on May 30, 2023 and described by the company as the purchase of Connect Topco Limited, a private Guernsey company, "in exchange for approximately $550.7 million in cash and 46.36 million shares of our common stock" (10-K page:6). The 10-K states total consideration of about USD 2.7 billion, comprising USD 2.1 billion of fair value of the shares and USD 550.7 million in cash, with goodwill of USD 1.5 billion in communication services (10-K page:169-170) and USD 31.3 million of transaction costs in FY2024. The financing of that deal and of Inmarsat since then is visible in the debt record: the 2023 Term Loan Facility of USD 616.7 million was entered into at the closing (10-Q June 2026 page:33), the 7.500% Senior Notes due 2031 of USD 733.4 million were issued in September 2023 to replace a USD 733.4 million unsecured bridge facility (page:42), Inmarsat amended its facilities in March 2024 to establish a USD 1.3 billion Inmarsat Term Loan Facility and a USD 550.0 million revolver (page:34), and certain Inmarsat Holdings subsidiaries issued USD 1.975 billion of 9.000% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 in September 2024 (page:41), the proceeds of which, with cash, redeemed all of the remaining USD 1.97 billion of Inmarsat 2026 Notes (10-K page:181). Status of the transaction: completed, with the share issuance of about 46.36 million shares and a role rationalization of about 800 positions that management announced as complete in November 2023 and describes as intended to achieve operational and cost efficiencies (10-K page:110; Management Language).

New debt and debt events in the periods since FY2025, all completed: in May 2025 the remaining USD 442.6 million of 5.625% Senior Notes due 2025 were redeemed at par (10-Q June 2026 page:38); in November 2025 the USD 300.0 million Original Inmarsat Term Loan was repaid early (page:34); on January 21, 2026 Viasat and ViaSat Technologies Limited entered into a USD 188.7 million direct loan facility with the Export-Import Bank of the United States, fully drawn at USD 188.7 million at March 31, 2026, repayable in 16 semi-annual installments from May 2026 to November 25, 2033 (10-Q Dec 2025 page:56; 10-K page:178); the former Ex-Im facility was repaid at maturity on October 15, 2025 (10-K page:178). No new debt was issued in Q1 FY2027 and no financing is described after June 30, 2026 in the sources. The use of proceeds for the Ex-Im facility is financing of ViaSat-3 F1 launch and insurance costs and exposure fees.

Disposals and receipts that affect liquidity: the Link-16 tactical data link sale for about USD 1.96 billion in cash completed in January 2023 (discontinued operations, 10-K page:133); the energy services system integration business divested in December 2024 (10-K page:111); the Navarino UK sale agreed in December 2025 and completed in March 2026 for USD 203.0 million of proceeds and a gain of USD 168.1 million, to a subsidiary of ICG (10-K page:110, page:133); and the Ligado settlement, under which a USD 420 million lump sum was received in October 2025, USD 100 million remains outstanding "pending resolution of certain matters", and quarterly payments of about USD 16 million with a 3% annual escalator began on September 30, 2025 (10-Q June 2026 page:46). Of the lump sum, USD 267.5 million was recorded as deferred revenue and USD 152.5 million as interest income (10-Q Dec 2025 page:52). A subsequent event after fiscal year end: a Cooperation Agreement dated May 6, 2026 between Viasat and Carronade Capital Management, LP and the persons on its Schedule A is listed as an exhibit filed with a report dated May 7, 2026 (10-K page:124); its terms, purpose and any board or governance changes are Not supplied. No merger, tender, spin-off, refinancing or sponsor transaction is described after June 30, 2026 in any source.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: services were 71% of FY2026 revenue, connectivity contracts require "advance or recurring monthly payments" (10-Q June 2026 page:6), firm backlog stood at USD 4,217.7 million, and aviation services revenue rose from USD 1,048,225 thousand to USD 1,191,426 thousand in FY2026 (10-K page:205). Risk mechanic: recurring service billing and a growing in-flight connectivity base (about 4,630 aircraft) support revenue visibility and cash conversion, but fixed services revenue fell from USD 741,601 thousand to USD 607,693 thousand as bandwidth was reallocated to aviation (10-K page:106), so growth depends on a shrinking consumer line being replaced. Credit implication: supports debt service capacity and refinancing access, tempered by capacity constraints before new satellites enter service; the backlog excludes future recurring IFC revenue (10-K page:108), so it understates aviation visibility. The Q1 FY2027 revenue decline (product revenues fell) is a counter-signal, small in size.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: capital expenditure of USD 992,774 thousand in FY2026, a USD 169.4 million impairment and other liabilities for the EMEA exit in FY2025, and in FY2024 a reduction of about USD 1.67 billion in the carrying value of satellites under construction, partly offset by about USD 770.0 million of insurance claim receivables (10-K page:137). Risk mechanic: owned-satellite capital intensity and launch or anomaly risk absorb cash flow ahead of revenue, and management itself expects higher operating costs before new satellites reach commercial service (10-Q June 2026 page:74). Credit implication: free cash flow depends on capital spending falling as satellites complete; FY2026 cash flow also benefited from the Ligado lump sum and the Navarino proceeds (CP-1), so run-rate debt service coverage is weaker than the headline. The ViaSat-3 F1 reflector issue is the documented precedent for execution risk.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: U.S. Government 16% of FY2026 revenue and five largest contracts 19%; "A majority of our contracts can be terminated at the convenience of the customer" (10-Q June 2026 page:69); DCAA is auditing fiscal 2025 incurred costs (page:9). Risk mechanic: government funding delays, audits and termination rights can interrupt cash receipts and revise revenue; a USD 15.1 million reserve exists for refunds. Credit implication: moderate concentration that matters most in a downturn or shutdown; no single commercial customer reaches 10%.

4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, repayment actions, no distributions beyond TrellisWare's minority. Risk mechanic: absent a controlling owner with a distribution incentive, leakage risk to creditors is low on documented actions, but ownership concentration and board rights are Not disclosed. Credit implication: alignment appears neutral to supportive on documented actions only; willingness is not inferred from identity. Counter-evidence: the Cooperation Agreement of May 2026 is unexplained and could alter board composition; its terms are Not supplied.

5. Structure and key uncertainties. Evidence: two debt groups with separate collateral and guarantors (CP-1), the Inmarsat revolver maturing March 28, 2027, the 2027 Notes in current debt, and a Viasat revolver with a springing maturity. Risk mechanic: creditor claims are structurally separated, so group-level cash and leverage drive recoveries and refinancing choices, and the springing date can remove revolver availability early. Credit implication: refinancing timing and group-level disclosure are the key uncertainties; recovery prospects cannot be assessed beyond noting the liens described, and no recovery conclusion is made.
### Conflicts and consistency with upstream

No conflict between sources was found on the facts used. Items checked: the Navarino sale date and amounts agree across the 10-K (page:110, page:133); the Ligado amounts agree across the 10-K, the December 2025 10-Q and the June 2026 10-Q; the Ex-Im facility amount agrees across the December 2025 10-Q (page:56) and the 10-K (page:178). No new calculation is made; every figure is a source figure or a CP-1 handoff figure. Counts: 7 issuer sources, 2 handoffs. - Not supplied: terms of the May 6, 2026 Cooperation Agreement; severity medium.
- Not supplied: credit ratings (the context lists none and the filings do not mention any); severity low for this module.

- Not supplied: shareholder letters and slides for the three results releases, which would carry management's operating narrative and any adjusted measures; the releases in the pack contain no operating content.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Viasat has deleveraged and holds ample liquidity, but operating income falls well short of interest expense, spending is heavy, and a USD 600.0 million secured-note maturity falls due by mid-2027. The credit view is adequate but exposed. | Medium | Derived EBITDA only, no covenant levels, no group-level data, and ownership and ratings are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Gross leverage is 4.58x and net leverage 3.37x on derived EBITDA, against 5.70x and 4.43x in FY2025. | Leverage has fallen, helped by lower debt and a weak FY2025 base. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 2,886.1 million, but the Inmarsat revolver expires in March 2027 and the Viasat revolver can mature early. | Cash covers near-term debt, yet part of the headline cushion is temporary. | High |
| Operating income of USD 108.8 million is far below interest expense of USD 342.2 million. | Coverage depends on EBITDA, so heavy depreciation and spending matter. | Medium |
| FY2026 cash flow and income include the Ligado lump sum and the Navarino gain. | Run-rate free cash flow is lower than the reported USD 597.1 million. | High |
| Debt sits in two groups, secured claims are large, and covenant and group data are missing. | Structural position and covenant headroom cannot be tested. | High |
### Credit view

Viasat's credit is adequate but exposed: debt has fallen and liquidity is ample, yet a USD 600.0 million secured-note maturity falls due by mid-2027 and cash generation depends on satellite spending easing. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,886.1 million and a recurring services base, with gross leverage down to 4.58x on derived EBITDA for the twelve months to June 2026 from 5.70x in FY2025. The weakest point is thin earnings after spending: derived EBITDA less capital expenditure was only 1.39x cash interest, and operating income covers just 0.32x of interest expense. What decides the outcome is whether the ViaSat-3 satellites lift revenue while capital spending of about USD 1.0 billion a year falls, and how the 2027 Notes and the Inmarsat revolver are refinanced.
### Key findings

1. Viasat's total debt was USD 6,570.5 million at June 30, 2026, down from USD 7,204.3 million at March 31, 2025, and gross leverage is 4.58x with net leverage 3.37x on derived, unadjusted EBITDA of USD 1,435.6 million for the twelve months, against 5.70x gross and 4.43x net in FY2025. Evidence is the CP-1 metrics; the mechanism is lower debt plus a recovery from the impairment-depressed FY2025 base, and the implication is a better leverage position that is still above 4x gross and has stalled since March 2026 (net debt USD 4,838.3 million then and USD 4,834.7 million now).

2. Liquidity is large but not all permanent. Cash of USD 1,735.8 million exceeds current debt of USD 661.9 million, and undrawn revolvers add USD 1,150.3 million, but the Inmarsat revolver of USD 550.0 million matures on March 28, 2027 and the Viasat revolver of USD 647.5 million carries a springing maturity tied to other material debt, with conditions the filings do not describe. The implication is that dependable liquidity after early 2027 is closer to cash plus whatever is extended.

3. The 5.625% Senior Secured Notes of USD 600.0 million are in current debt at June 30, 2026, and the fiscal-year schedule places them between April and June 2027 by inference. The larger wall follows: USD 3,246.7 million falls in FY2030 and USD 1,341.3 million in FY2031. Refinancing access and cost matter because the Inmarsat term loan and notes carry effective or stated rates of about 9%.

4. Earnings are thin after capital intensity. Derived EBITDA covers cash interest 4.73x and interest expense 4.20x, but after capital expenditure of USD 1,013.7 million the remaining USD 421.9 million is only 1.39x cash interest of USD 303.7 million, and operating income of USD 108.8 million covers 0.32x of interest expense of USD 342.2 million. Depreciation of USD 1,014.5 million and amortization of USD 312.3 million carry the gap. The implication is that debt service relies on spending discipline and on new satellites adding revenue.

5. The reported cash flow flatters the run-rate. FY2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,589.9 million includes the Ligado lump sum of USD 420.0 million, leaving about USD 177.1 million of free cash flow for FY2026 and about USD 158.3 million for the twelve months, against reported USD 597.1 million and USD 578.3 million. FY2026 other income also includes the USD 168.1 million Navarino gain, which is outside derived EBITDA. A further USD 100 million Ligado payment remains outstanding with no collection date.

6. Business risk is moderate. Services are 71% of FY2026 revenue and firm backlog is USD 4,217.7 million, aviation services revenue rose in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027, and no commercial customer reaches 10% of revenue; against that, the U.S. Government is 16% of FY2026 revenue, the five largest contracts are 19%, product revenue fell in Q1 FY2027, and derived EBITDA for Q1 FY2027 was USD 361.3 million against USD 388.3 million a year earlier. Satellite execution risk is documented by the FY2024 ViaSat-3 F1 reflector issue, which led to a net loss of about USD 905.5 million after insurance receivables.

7. Structure and behaviour. Of the USD 6,570.5 million, USD 5,294.4 million is secured term debt, notes and the Ex-Im loan, USD 1,133.4 million is senior unsecured notes and USD 142.7 million is finance leases, split between a Viasat group and an Inmarsat group with separate collateral and guarantors. The documented behaviour is supportive for creditors: notes redeemed, an Inmarsat term loan repaid early, no dividends ever declared, no sponsor or controlling holder identified. Ownership shares, ratings and the May 2026 Cooperation Agreement terms are not supplied, so willingness is judged on actions only.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Deleveraging: total debt is USD 633.8 million lower than at March 2025 and derived coverage of cash interest rose from 3.24x to 4.73x (Documentary Fact, CP-1 figures; the ratios are derived, so read as Analyst Interpretation of filed lines). (2) Liquidity: USD 2,886.1 million, with cash covering all USD 661.9 million of current debt and leaving USD 1,073.9 million after it (Documentary Fact). (3) Recurring services base and backlog: services are 71% of revenue, connectivity is billed in advance or monthly, and firm backlog is USD 4,217.7 million (Documentary Fact; the backlog excludes future recurring in-flight connectivity revenue, so visibility is understated). (4) Customer breadth: no commercial customer at 10% of revenue and the in-flight connectivity base of about 4,630 aircraft is growing (Documentary Fact). (5) Segment balance: defense and advanced technologies earned segment operating profit of USD 216.3 million in FY2026, steady with the prior year, beside a communication services swing to profit that mainly reflects the absence of the FY2025 EMEA impairment (Documentary Fact). (6) Creditor-supportive actions: debt repaid and no dividends (Documentary Fact for the actions; the inference that they signal willingness is Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. (1) Near-term maturities and expiries: USD 600.0 million of secured notes by mid-2027, the Inmarsat revolver in March 2027 and the Viasat revolver springing date (Documentary Fact, with the notes' window an inference). (2) Capital intensity: capital expenditure of USD 992.8 million in FY2026 and free cash flow of negative USD 122.0 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact); the dependence of cash generation on spending falling is Analyst Interpretation. (3) Thin earnings after depreciation: operating income of USD 108.8 million against interest expense of USD 342.2 million (Documentary Fact, derived ratio). (4) One-off support in FY2026: the Ligado lump sum and the Navarino gain (Documentary Fact). (5) Structure: two debt groups, secured debt ahead of USD 1,133.4 million of unsecured notes, floating-rate term loans of USD 2,542.5 million at effective rates between 8.86% and 9.38% (Documentary Fact). (6) Concentration: the U.S. Government at 16% and the five largest contracts at 19% (Documentary Fact), with termination-for-convenience rights described by management (Management Language, qualified). (7) Visibility gaps: no company-defined EBITDA, covenant levels or group-level financials (Insufficient Information; missing evidence is not read as adverse).
### Assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Adequate but exposed: improved leverage and ample liquidity against a close refinancing, thin post-capital-expenditure cover and heavy capital intensity | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, coverage, liquidity and maturity figures; CP-1A business and behaviour facts |

| Thesis | Viasat can service its debt from recurring connectivity and defense revenue and from large cash balances, but only if satellite spending falls and the 2027 maturities are refinanced on acceptable terms | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same |

Confidence is below High because the CP-1A readiness judgment for this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and because EBITDA is derived, covenant levels and group-level data are absent, and ownership and ratings are not supplied.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Refinancing of the 2027 Notes and the revolvers | The USD 600.0 million notes are current; the Inmarsat revolver expires March 28, 2027; the Viasat revolver can mature about 91 days before certain material debt unless conditions are met | Liquidity and refinancing pressure in 2027 if markets or covenant headroom are weak | Material |

| Satellite execution and capital intensity | Launch, deployment or anomaly risk (the FY2024 F1 reflector issue) and capital spending of about USD 1.0 billion a year delay revenue while debt service continues | Free cash flow and leverage reduction slow or reverse | Material |

| Earnings quality | EBITDA is unadjusted and includes impairment effects in FY2025; FY2026 cash flow includes the Ligado lump sum; operating income is small against interest | Reported coverage overstates sustainable capacity | Material |

| Interest cost and rate exposure | Floating-rate term loans of USD 2,542.5 million at about 9% effective rates and notes at 9.000% (Inmarsat) and 7.500% | A rise in benchmark rates or a failed refinancing increases cash interest | Material |

| Government concentration | The U.S. Government is 16% of revenue and the five largest contracts 19%; contracts can be terminated for convenience; audits are open | Receipts or revenue can be interrupted in a funding disruption | Minor |

| Structural separation and covenant visibility | Separate Viasat and Inmarsat collateral and guarantors; maintenance tests exist but levels and group data are not supplied | Cash access, covenant headroom and creditor control by group cannot be tested | Material |

| Unresolved receivable and tax items | USD 100 million Ligado payment outstanding with no collection date; unrecognized tax benefits of USD 230.9 million | Possible cash or earnings volatility | Minor |
### Gaps ledger
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Company-defined EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and add-back schedule not supplied | All coverage and leverage here are derived and unadjusted | Leverage, coverage, FCF | Medium | Obtain results letters and slides; label derived measures |

| Covenant levels, definitions and reported ratios not supplied; agreements not supplied | Headroom and default risk cannot be assessed | Covenant view, structure | High | Obtain credit agreements and indentures |
| Group-level financials and cash location for Viasat and Inmarsat not supplied | Debt serviceability and cash access differ by group | Leverage by group, liquidity | High | Obtain group disclosure |

| Day and month maturities of the 2027, 2028, Inmarsat 2029 and 2031 Notes, and the revolver springing conditions, not supplied | Refinancing timing and revolver availability | Maturity wall, liquidity | Medium | Obtain indentures and the revolver agreement |

| Ownership percentages, board control, ratings and the May 2026 Cooperation Agreement not supplied | Sponsor alignment and control cannot be judged beyond documented actions | Governance view | Medium | Obtain the proxy statement, the Cooperation Agreement and rating reports |

| Evidence after June 30, 2026 | The pack ends with the June 2026 quarter; ViaSat-3 service starts, refinancing or ownership events after that date are not evidenced | All conclusions | Medium | Obtain later filings or releases before reliance |
| Q4 FY2026 and quarterly cash flows are derived by difference | Quarterly trends are approximate | Trend analysis | Low | Use the derived bridge with its label |
## Calculations
Inputs are CP-1 figures (USD million; thousands in brackets where used) and CP-1A facts.
1. Total debt change: 7,204.3 - 6,570.5 = 633.8. Net debt change since March 2026: 4,838.3 - 4,834.7 = 3.6.

2. Derived EBITDA less capital expenditure (purchases of property, equipment and satellites, and other assets), then divided by cash interest: LTM 1,435.6 - 1,013.7 = 421.9 (1,435,586 - 1,013,689 = 421,897 thousand) and 421,897 / 303,748 = 1.39x; FY2026 1,462,590 - 992,774 = 469,816 and 469,816 / 326,548 = 1.44x; FY2025 1,263,327 - 1,030,182 = 233,145 and 233,145 / 390,043 = 0.60x.
3. Operating income to interest expense, LTM: 108,761 / 342,197 = 0.32x.

5. Debt composition at June 30, 2026 (USD thousand, CP-1 table): secured = 2022 Term Loan 672,000 + 2023 Term Loan 599,741 + Inmarsat Term Loan 1,270,750 + Ex-Im 176,934 + 2027 Notes 600,000 + Inmarsat 2029 Notes 1,975,000 = 5,294,425; senior unsecured = 2028 Notes 400,000 + 2031 Notes 733,400 = 1,133,400; finance leases 142,678; total 5,294,425 + 1,133,400 + 142,678 = 6,570,503. Floating-rate term loans = 672,000 + 599,741 + 1,270,750 = 2,542,491. This is a composition fact by instrument, not a recovery conclusion; finance lease security is not stated in the handoff, and the Viasat revolver is undrawn.
6. Q1 FY2027 derived EBITDA against Q1 FY2026: 361,334 - 388,338 = -27,004 thousand (USD 27.0 million lower).
7. Free cash flow before the Ligado lump sum (CP-1 sensitivity): FY2026 597.1 - 420.0 = 177.1; LTM 578.3 - 420.0 = 158.3.
## Gaps
- The credit view is on derived and unadjusted measures, not on company-defined or covenant measures; headroom is Not calculable.

- Unresolved: group-level leverage; whether the Viasat revolver springing maturity will bind (conditions not described); the maturity day of the 2027 Notes (inferred to April to June 2027 from the fiscal-year schedule and the current classification).
- Not supplied: ownership percentages, ratings, the Cooperation Agreement terms, results letters and slides, credit agreements and indentures.
- Nothing after June 30, 2026 is evidenced, although the as-of date is 2026-11-05: events such as satellite service starts are Management Language and expectations, not results.

- No conflict between the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs was found. CP-1A refines CP-0 by noting that the June 2026 10-Q also lists the Cooperation Agreement exhibit; this module relies on CP-1A for that point.
## Next module

CP-5 should trace the material claims in this credit view to their evidence, in particular the derived ratios (leverage 4.58x, coverage 4.73x, 1.39x after capital expenditure, 0.32x operating income to interest), the liquidity build of USD 2,886.1 million, the debt composition, and the Ligado and Navarino items. Relative value and the committee's action belong to later modules and are not addressed here.

### Evidence trace view

The evidence trace for Viasat is sound on figures and weaker on definitions. Every reported amount in the earlier handoffs was found in the filings, a few under the wrong page, and every derived ratio recomputed to the same value. The one inference, the April to June 2027 window for the USD 600.0 million 2027 Notes, is labelled as an inference. The weakest point is the debt basis: leverage is stated on principal, while carrying value gives 4.49x gross and 3.28x net for the twelve months to June 2026, against 4.58x and 3.37x. Covenant levels, company-defined EBITDA, ownership percentages and ratings cannot be traced because no source supplies them. Committee use is restricted until the carrying-value variant is shown and the citation slips are corrected.

Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 2 are directly sourced, 3 are calculated, 0 are assumption-based, 0 are analyst inferences, and 0 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of covenant definitions, levels and a company-defined EBITDA, which matters because every leverage and coverage figure is derived from filed lines and cannot be tested against the tests that govern default, and which implies that committee use is restricted to the derived view until the credit agreements are supplied.

CLEARANCE DECISION: Pass with Remediation. Critical Issues: 0. Material Issues: 1. Minor Issues: 7. Committee Use: Restricted.

No figure was found to be wrong. The Material issue is a definition drift: CP-1 and CP-2 state leverage on debt principal, while the carrying-value basis is the governing balance-sheet basis, and the variant should be shown beside the principal figures. The seven Minor issues are locator, precision, style and transport points listed in the issue log. QA status under the severity engine: Restricted. The confidence score was not computed with the deterministic script, which is not available in this host session; the band is Medium.
### Remediation priority map
